correctness.rationale: Unfolding the named-extension rank leaves one root v, one partner w_i per root state i, and all q^2 ordered extension profiles at every pair (v,w_i). In class B_j, fullness for w_j requires q distinct vertices other than w_j, so |B_j|>=q+1. There are at least q^2-1 supported root pairs, and q^2(q-1) supported partner-to-class incidences away from the root. The only double counts are supported pairs between partners, at most binom(q,2); equality also rules out uncounted supported pairs. At minimum order, within each partner's own class the q peripheral vertices are uniquely labelled by the q states. For i!=j, the supported pair w_i w_j fills one of the q-1 nonzero states and the remaining q-2 are injected into q peripheral slots, leaving two zeros. These choices are independent and consistent under converse. A certificate-preserving isomorphism fixes all state labels, so the count is the product stated, not an unpointed census. Adding genuine zero-state isolates preserves the witness at all larger orders. q=2 gives (7,6,1), and q=3 gives (13,23,5832).
residual_risks: The supplied finite enumeration and deletion checks are corroboration, not a proof of the universal bound; the checker was not executed in this review. No unpointed q=3 census or classification at larger orders is asserted.

value.rationale: Defines the sharp finite resources for simultaneous realization of all third moves in the free state class. Optimizing nonzero support separately from host order is a substantive extremal question: sharing between designated partners is exactly the correction term, and the equality argument gives a useful structural classification and exact pointed census rather than just a construction or an exhaustive run at one q.
residual_risks: The classification counts certificates; it does not collapse them to unpointed structures or answer higher-round questions.
